name: Default Professional Resume
description: Single-voice, employer-neutral resume template: one applicant voice, flagship credits first, honest capability gaps, ATS-safe print styles.

themeSync.note: External palette kits can be mapped into the default-resume.json token names, then mirrored into default-resume.css without changing Letter geometry.

layout.screenPreview: Use visible Letter-sized wrappers (8.5in x 11in) so page breaks can be reviewed before export.
layout.footer: Optional fixed print footer. Reserve bottom space through @page margins and page breaks.

paths.note: html_to_pdf.py writes here by default when no explicit output PDF is passed; use --output-dir or a full output path to override.

exportModes.darkPdf: Run html_to_pdf.py with --pdf-theme dark; template must include html[data-pdf-theme="dark"] print overrides.
exportModes.bundlePdf: Run merge_pdfs.py final-application.pdf cover-letter.pdf resume.pdf --require-letter when a portal accepts one upload.
exportModes.png: Render generated PDFs to page PNG files with pdf_to_png.py.

sections.title: Profile
sections.data: one applicant voice, 3-5 sentence summary, no target-employer name

sections.title: Core Capabilities
sections.data: grouped skill categories, pulled from vault claims

sections.title: Selected Credits
sections.data: flagship items first (by your own ranking), then supporting credits

sections.title: About
sections.data: single bio paragraph, same voice as Profile

sections.title: Technology
sections.data: stack list + an explicit honest-gap note for anything unverified

_note: This profile's live reference render IS default-resume.html. resume-source.example.json documents the claim-vault schema this template's content should be tailored from — copy both, replace with your own verified claims, and keep the real copies out of version control (see ../../../.gitignore).
